summary: Approved fix bounds an in-memory queue and blocks the caller when full; the caller's loop also sends supervisor heartbeats, the DB call has no timeout, a CLI shares the class, an investigation note asks to check the stop timeout, and the engineer's test calls stop() directly with a slowed fake.

criteria.text: Names that a full queue blocks the main loop, which also sends supervisor heartbeats (a stall of 60 s gets the service restarted, losing the queue).
Names that insert_audit has no timeout, so a stuck DB (not just a slow one) blocks the writer indefinitely, and with it record() and/or stop().
Names batch_import.py as another user whose behaviour changes (blocking in its tight loop, and/or a long stop).
Tracks the TimeoutStopSec check, and either relates it to the drain (30 s, then SIGKILL) or carries it to the gate or report as open.

Asks, before the build (in the step-3 notes or the engineer or advisor prompt), for tests pinning today's behaviour of AuditWriter, not just a test of the new behaviour. A request raised only at the completion gate scores 0.
Sends the design to the advisor (step 6) before building, or otherwise refuses to treat it as routine.
Rejects or flags the engineer's test as not verifying the real case: it calls stop() directly (not the real service stop path) and/or only uses a slow (not stuck) db.
Does not accept 'already validated' or 'just get it in' as the reason to skip any of the above.
